content.value: Five properties, in the user's words — simple, safe, smooth, clever, everywhere. Each is testable, not a slogan:

items.text: One command joins the fleet; one hands it a wish. No message bus, no bespoke console. An order is just a task.
items.title: Simple

items.text: A fence never fails to isolate; a worker never self-merges; a runaway never OOMs a neighbour; a spend cap always halts. Safe to leave running overnight.
items.title: Safe

items.text: Idle costs nothing; work wakes a listener instantly; a dead worker recovers itself; the operator sees everything at a glance.
items.title: Smooth

items.text: Every order lands on the cheapest sufficient box; idle capacity becomes deeper ambition; the ledger computes the collision math.
items.title: Clever

items.text: Identical on a laptop and across cloud support servers; identical for Claude, Codex, or any MCP/shell agent. One protocol, many homes.
items.title: Everywhere

Codex ran the full contract on the same ledger, criteria 1/1
bp listen (SSE) · bp task frontier · bp cmux · bp mcp serve — all shipped

content.value: A worker that backgrounds its work produces nothing (fixed: in-turn rule). The fence lifecycle bug —
close
does not free a claim's resources (
task-fence-lifecycle-three-defects
) — is worked around with unique fences and is a named wave below. These are known, not lurking.

blocks.title: And the scars we already paid for

content.value: Six things stand between the working PoC and a fleet you would leave running for a week:

items.label: Gap 1
items.text: No native way to declare a listener and see the live fleet. The one missing CLI primitive.

items.label: Gap 2
items.text: The router is proven but not yet fed by live listener capacity. Sizes are declared, not sensed.

items.label: Gap 3
items.text: Adding a support server is hand-run; it should be one action, migration-invariant.

items.label: Gap 4
items.text: Resident listeners are fragile to drive; lease-lapse recovery and the fence bug are unfixed.

items.label: Gap 5
items.text: The conductor is smart per-wish but has no standing spend cap, work-source dials, or scale limits.

items.label: Gap 6
items.text: No single end-to-end run has proven the whole thing perfect, unattended, at size.

content.value: Each wave closes one gap, ships behind a proof, and leaves the fleet more perfect than it found it. Waves A–B are the core; C–E harden and scale; F seals.

blocks.text: Wave A — Presence & roster (the one native gap)

items.text: A listener schema (worker · status · scope · capacity · last-seen, TTL'd) on the Herd report_state substrate; bp fleet listen <name> (register + heartbeat + consume) and bp fleet roster (the orchestrator's live view). Skills adopt the native verbs.
items.title: Build

items.text: You cannot conduct what you cannot see. Every later wave (routing, cloud, durability) reads the roster.
items.title: Why first

blocks.text: Wave B — Close the efficiency loop

items.text: Listeners measure and advertise their size class + free slots + budget in the presence heartbeat; the orchestrator feeds the live roster to route.py. Idle-capacity-as-permission and the hard spend cap become live, not designed.
items.title: Build

items.text: The clever core goes real: a 32 GB box is reserved for the export, lean boxes soak up the rest — measured, not guessed.
items.title: Payoff

blocks.text: Wave C — Cloud add-support, one action

items.text: One console/CLI action: provision a support server (site-spawner / instance lifecycle / Hetzner client), bind it to the main, scrubbed-pull its dataset (the PDS data plane), and start a listener. The migration invariant made real — two strings, zero protocol.
items.title: Build

items.text: Scaling the fleet becomes a click, and neighbour noise ends at the machine boundary.
items.title: Payoff

items.text: Fix the fence lifecycle bug (close frees resources; release works on done) and retire the unique-fence workaround. Lease-lapse recovery (a dead worker's orders re-open). Resident-listener robustness or the durable headless-per-order runner as the default. The spend cap that halts cycles, wired to the meter.
items.title: Build

items.text: Safe to leave alone: a wedged or dead worker self-heals; a runaway is braked; no fence ever deadlocks.
items.title: Payoff

blocks.text: Wave E — Orchestrator intelligence at scale

items.text: The work-source dials (backlog · wish · auto, auto gated on a measured multiplier); the autonomy dial (full · tiered · manual) with the merge arbiter for code orders; ambition that scales with idle capacity and retreats under failure. Gate hardening so full-auto's greens are non-vacuous.
items.title: Build

items.text: The conductor becomes genuinely efficient and genuinely safe at 5, 10, 20 concurrent orders.
items.title: Payoff

items.text: One unattended end-to-end run: a real wish, decomposed and routed across differently-sized cloud + local listeners of MIXED agent kinds (Claude + Codex), fence-safe, honestly graded, no babysitting — with the field guide walked by a stranger. The proof that it is perfect.
items.title: Build

items.text: The epic closes on evidence, not assertion.
items.title: Payoff

blocks.text: Proof obligations — every wave must be able to fail

content.value: A green that a broken build could also produce proves nothing. Each wave ships with a proof that fires only when the thing actually works:

rows.value: Two listeners register; the roster shows both; kill one and it flips to OFFLINE past its TTL — not before
A heavy order lands on the big box and a light one does NOT, driven by live heartbeats; over-cap work is flagged, not dropped
One action produces a live listener on a fresh cloud box that claims and closes a real order; teardown leaves nothing
close frees a fence (re-claimable immediately); a killed worker's order re-opens; the spend cap halts a running batch
Full-auto merges only gate-green work a broken build could not fake; tiered blocks a core-path change for human sign-off
A stranger runs the guide unaided; mixed-agent, mixed-size fleet completes a real wish unattended and grades honestly

items.text: Retired by fences (bp task frontier) + the serial merge arbiter. THE risk; addressed first-class in Waves A/E.
items.title: Merge storms

items.text: Retired by the fleet-wide meter + spend-cap-as-zero-ambition (Wave D). Never bundle unbounded tokens.
items.title: Runaway spend

items.text: Retired by the proof-must-fire obligation on every wave, and sealed grading in the orchestrator.
items.title: Vacuous greens

items.text: Retired by disposability + lease-lapse recovery + durable runner (Wave D): kill and restart loses nothing.
items.title: Fragile automation

items.text: Already retired: provider-neutral core, Claude + Codex proven, one adapter line per new agent.
items.title: Vendor lock

items.text: Retired at the machine boundary (Wave C): heavy work on a cloud support never touches the responsive main.
items.title: Neighbour noise

snapshot.title: Done · PoC + skills + router + Codex proof

content.value: Run each wave through
bp-epic-cycle
— the fleet builds itself the way it will build everything else — under the epic task
task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5
. Waves A and B are the shortest path to a fleet that is both visible and efficient; C–E can proceed in parallel once the roster exists.

items.value: Join in one command.
Any agent, any machine:
fleet-run.sh listen <name>
or the skill — and it appears in the roster.
Conduct in one wish.
Hand the orchestrator a goal; it decomposes, routes by size, dispatches, and grades — with nothing to babysit.
Never a collision, never a runaway.
Fences hold; the arbiter serialises; the spend cap brakes.
Cloud and local are one.
The same protocol, the same commands, the machine boundary the only real difference.
Sealed by a real run.
Wave F's unattended, mixed-agent, mixed-size proof — the epic closes on it.

content.value: The ledger is the bus · a fence is a lease · presence is a heartbeat · the router is best-fit · the machine is the isolation boundary.
Every wave is one of these five made more perfect. Nothing else is load-bearing.

PERSONAL DEV FLEET · THE BUILD PLAN

The Road to a Perfect Dev Fleet

Barkpark · Personal Dev Fleet epic · Build plan · Rev 1 · 2026-07-21

The PoC is proven: listeners and an orchestrator, orders as tasks, fences that refuse collisions, honest sealed grading — and it runs Claude Code and Codex alike. This is the engineering plan that carries it from proven to perfect: a fleet that is simple to run, safe to leave alone, ruthlessly efficient across resource sizes, and identical on a laptop or across the cloud. Six waves, each with a non-vacuous proof it must pass.

Perfect is not more features. Perfect is: one command to join, a fence that never fails, a big box never wasted, and nothing to babysit.

6
Waves to perfect
2
Agents proven (Claude + Codex)
8/8
Router proof today
~80%
CLI protocol already shipped
1
Native gap: presence/roster
5
Ideas the whole design rests on
  1. 1. What perfect means
  2. 2. Where we stand — the receipts
  3. 3. The gap: proven → perfect
  4. 4. The six waves
  5. 5. Proof obligations
  6. 6. Risks, each retired
  7. 7. The sequence
  8. 8. Definition of done

What perfect means

Five properties, in the user's words — simple, safe, smooth, clever, everywhere. Each is testable, not a slogan:

Simple
One command joins the fleet; one hands it a wish. No message bus, no bespoke console. An order is just a task.
Safe
A fence never fails to isolate; a worker never self-merges; a runaway never OOMs a neighbour; a spend cap always halts. Safe to leave running overnight.
Smooth
Idle costs nothing; work wakes a listener instantly; a dead worker recovers itself; the operator sees everything at a glance.
Clever
Every order lands on the cheapest sufficient box; idle capacity becomes deeper ambition; the ledger computes the collision math.
Everywhere
Identical on a laptop and across cloud support servers; identical for Claude, Codex, or any MCP/shell agent. One protocol, many homes.

Where we stand — the receipts

This plan starts from proven ground, not hope. Every row below has a live receipt:

ProvenEvidence
Orders as tasks; claim/stamp/close loopPoC rounds 1–2; resident + headless listeners
Fences refuse collisions409 resource_conflict fired live 3×; bp task frontier ships the allocator
Orchestrator decomposes + grades honestly4-challenge 2-step campaign, sealed answer keys, 3/4 PASS
Resource-size routingroute.py self-test 8/8 — best-fit across tiny/lean/big
Provider-neutralCodex ran the full contract on the same ledger, criteria 1/1
CLI substratebp listen (SSE) · bp task frontier · bp cmux · bp mcp serve — all shipped
Skills + runnerfleet-listener, fleet-orchestrator, tooling/fleet/fleet-run.sh — merged
And the scars we already paid for
A worker that backgrounds its work produces nothing (fixed: in-turn rule). The fence lifecycle bug — close does not free a claim's resources (task-fence-lifecycle-three-defects) — is worked around with unique fences and is a named wave below. These are known, not lurking.

The gap: proven → perfect

Six things stand between the working PoC and a fleet you would leave running for a week:

Gap 1Presence & roster No native way to declare a listener and see the live fleet. The one missing CLI primitive.
Gap 2Efficiency loop open The router is proven but not yet fed by live listener capacity. Sizes are declared, not sensed.
Gap 3Cloud onboarding manual Adding a support server is hand-run; it should be one action, migration-invariant.
Gap 4Durability Resident listeners are fragile to drive; lease-lapse recovery and the fence bug are unfixed.
Gap 5Orchestrator ceiling The conductor is smart per-wish but has no standing spend cap, work-source dials, or scale limits.
Gap 6No seal No single end-to-end run has proven the whole thing perfect, unattended, at size.

The six waves

Each wave closes one gap, ships behind a proof, and leaves the fleet more perfect than it found it. Waves A–B are the core; C–E harden and scale; F seals.

Wave A — Presence & roster (the one native gap)

Build
A listener schema (worker · status · scope · capacity · last-seen, TTL'd) on the Herd report_state substrate; bp fleet listen <name> (register + heartbeat + consume) and bp fleet roster (the orchestrator's live view). Skills adopt the native verbs.
Why first
You cannot conduct what you cannot see. Every later wave (routing, cloud, durability) reads the roster.

Wave B — Close the efficiency loop

Build
Listeners measure and advertise their size class + free slots + budget in the presence heartbeat; the orchestrator feeds the live roster to route.py. Idle-capacity-as-permission and the hard spend cap become live, not designed.
Payoff
The clever core goes real: a 32 GB box is reserved for the export, lean boxes soak up the rest — measured, not guessed.

Wave C — Cloud add-support, one action

Build
One console/CLI action: provision a support server (site-spawner / instance lifecycle / Hetzner client), bind it to the main, scrubbed-pull its dataset (the PDS data plane), and start a listener. The migration invariant made real — two strings, zero protocol.
Payoff
Scaling the fleet becomes a click, and neighbour noise ends at the machine boundary.

Wave D — Durability & safety hardening

Build
Fix the fence lifecycle bug (close frees resources; release works on done) and retire the unique-fence workaround. Lease-lapse recovery (a dead worker's orders re-open). Resident-listener robustness or the durable headless-per-order runner as the default. The spend cap that halts cycles, wired to the meter.
Payoff
Safe to leave alone: a wedged or dead worker self-heals; a runaway is braked; no fence ever deadlocks.

Wave E — Orchestrator intelligence at scale

Build
The work-source dials (backlog · wish · auto, auto gated on a measured multiplier); the autonomy dial (full · tiered · manual) with the merge arbiter for code orders; ambition that scales with idle capacity and retreats under failure. Gate hardening so full-auto's greens are non-vacuous.
Payoff
The conductor becomes genuinely efficient and genuinely safe at 5, 10, 20 concurrent orders.

Wave F — The seal

Build
One unattended end-to-end run: a real wish, decomposed and routed across differently-sized cloud + local listeners of MIXED agent kinds (Claude + Codex), fence-safe, honestly graded, no babysitting — with the field guide walked by a stranger. The proof that it is perfect.
Payoff
The epic closes on evidence, not assertion.

Proof obligations — every wave must be able to fail

A green that a broken build could also produce proves nothing. Each wave ships with a proof that fires only when the thing actually works:

WaveThe proof that must fire
ATwo listeners register; the roster shows both; kill one and it flips to OFFLINE past its TTL — not before
BA heavy order lands on the big box and a light one does NOT, driven by live heartbeats; over-cap work is flagged, not dropped
COne action produces a live listener on a fresh cloud box that claims and closes a real order; teardown leaves nothing
Dclose frees a fence (re-claimable immediately); a killed worker's order re-opens; the spend cap halts a running batch
EFull-auto merges only gate-green work a broken build could not fake; tiered blocks a core-path change for human sign-off
FA stranger runs the guide unaided; mixed-agent, mixed-size fleet completes a real wish unattended and grades honestly

Risks, each retired

Merge storms
Retired by fences (bp task frontier) + the serial merge arbiter. THE risk; addressed first-class in Waves A/E.
Runaway spend
Retired by the fleet-wide meter + spend-cap-as-zero-ambition (Wave D). Never bundle unbounded tokens.
Vacuous greens
Retired by the proof-must-fire obligation on every wave, and sealed grading in the orchestrator.
Fragile automation
Retired by disposability + lease-lapse recovery + durable runner (Wave D): kill and restart loses nothing.
Vendor lock
Already retired: provider-neutral core, Claude + Codex proven, one adapter line per new agent.
Neighbour noise
Retired at the machine boundary (Wave C): heavy work on a cloud support never touches the responsive main.

The sequence

ProvenCoreHardenSeal
Done · PoC + skills + router + Codex proof
 
A · Presence & roster
 
B · Efficiency loop
 
C · Cloud add-support
 
D · Durability & safety
 
E · Orchestrator at scale
 
F · The seal
 

Run each wave through bp-epic-cycle — the fleet builds itself the way it will build everything else — under the epic task task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5. Waves A and B are the shortest path to a fleet that is both visible and efficient; C–E can proceed in parallel once the roster exists.

Definition of done

1. Join in one command. Any agent, any machine: fleet-run.sh listen <name> or the skill — and it appears in the roster.
2. Conduct in one wish. Hand the orchestrator a goal; it decomposes, routes by size, dispatches, and grades — with nothing to babysit.
3. Never a collision, never a runaway. Fences hold; the arbiter serialises; the spend cap brakes.
4. Cloud and local are one. The same protocol, the same commands, the machine boundary the only real difference.
5. Sealed by a real run. Wave F's unattended, mixed-agent, mixed-size proof — the epic closes on it.
The five ideas the whole plan rests on
The ledger is the bus · a fence is a lease · presence is a heartbeat · the router is best-fit · the machine is the isolation boundary. Every wave is one of these five made more perfect. Nothing else is load-bearing.

Fences refuse collisions409 resource_conflict fired live 3×; bp task frontier ships the allocator
Orchestrator decomposes + grades honestly4-challenge 2-step campaign, sealed answer keys, 3/4 PASS
Resource-size routingroute.py self-test 8/8 — best-fit across tiny/lean/big
Provider-neutralCodex ran the full contract on the same ledger, criteria 1/1
CLI substratebp listen (SSE) · bp task frontier · bp cmux · bp mcp serve — all shipped
Skills + runnerfleet-listener, fleet-orchestrator, tooling/fleet/fleet-run.sh — merged
And the scars we already paid for A worker that backgrounds its work produces nothing (fixed: in-turn rule). The fence lifecycle bug — close does not free a claim's resources (task-fence-lifecycle-three-defects) — is worked around with unique fences and is a named wave below. These are known, not lurking.
§

The gap: proven → perfect

Six things stand between the working PoC and a fleet you would leave running for a week:

Gap 1
Presence & roster No native way to declare a listener and see the live fleet. The one missing CLI primitive.
Gap 2
Efficiency loop open The router is proven but not yet fed by live listener capacity. Sizes are declared, not sensed.
Gap 3
Cloud onboarding manual Adding a support server is hand-run; it should be one action, migration-invariant.
Gap 4
Durability Resident listeners are fragile to drive; lease-lapse recovery and the fence bug are unfixed.
Gap 5
Orchestrator ceiling The conductor is smart per-wish but has no standing spend cap, work-source dials, or scale limits.
Gap 6
No seal No single end-to-end run has proven the whole thing perfect, unattended, at size.
§

The six waves

Each wave closes one gap, ships behind a proof, and leaves the fleet more perfect than it found it. Waves A–B are the core; C–E harden and scale; F seals.

Wave A — Presence & roster (the one native gap)

Build
A listener schema (worker · status · scope · capacity · last-seen, TTL'd) on the Herd report_state substrate; bp fleet listen <name> (register + heartbeat + consume) and bp fleet roster (the orchestrator's live view). Skills adopt the native verbs.
Why first
You cannot conduct what you cannot see. Every later wave (routing, cloud, durability) reads the roster.

Wave B — Close the efficiency loop

Build
Listeners measure and advertise their size class + free slots + budget in the presence heartbeat; the orchestrator feeds the live roster to route.py. Idle-capacity-as-permission and the hard spend cap become live, not designed.
Payoff
The clever core goes real: a 32 GB box is reserved for the export, lean boxes soak up the rest — measured, not guessed.

Wave C — Cloud add-support, one action

Build
One console/CLI action: provision a support server (site-spawner / instance lifecycle / Hetzner client), bind it to the main, scrubbed-pull its dataset (the PDS data plane), and start a listener. The migration invariant made real — two strings, zero protocol.
Payoff
Scaling the fleet becomes a click, and neighbour noise ends at the machine boundary.

Wave D — Durability & safety hardening

Build
Fix the fence lifecycle bug (close frees resources; release works on done) and retire the unique-fence workaround. Lease-lapse recovery (a dead worker's orders re-open). Resident-listener robustness or the durable headless-per-order runner as the default. The spend cap that halts cycles, wired to the meter.
Payoff
Safe to leave alone: a wedged or dead worker self-heals; a runaway is braked; no fence ever deadlocks.

Wave E — Orchestrator intelligence at scale

Build
The work-source dials (backlog · wish · auto, auto gated on a measured multiplier); the autonomy dial (full · tiered · manual) with the merge arbiter for code orders; ambition that scales with idle capacity and retreats under failure. Gate hardening so full-auto's greens are non-vacuous.
Payoff
The conductor becomes genuinely efficient and genuinely safe at 5, 10, 20 concurrent orders.

Wave F — The seal

Build
One unattended end-to-end run: a real wish, decomposed and routed across differently-sized cloud + local listeners of MIXED agent kinds (Claude + Codex), fence-safe, honestly graded, no babysitting — with the field guide walked by a stranger. The proof that it is perfect.
Payoff
The epic closes on evidence, not assertion.
§

Proof obligations — every wave must be able to fail

A green that a broken build could also produce proves nothing. Each wave ships with a proof that fires only when the thing actually works:

WaveThe proof that must fire
ATwo listeners register; the roster shows both; kill one and it flips to OFFLINE past its TTL — not before
BA heavy order lands on the big box and a light one does NOT, driven by live heartbeats; over-cap work is flagged, not dropped
COne action produces a live listener on a fresh cloud box that claims and closes a real order; teardown leaves nothing
Dclose frees a fence (re-claimable immediately); a killed worker's order re-opens; the spend cap halts a running batch
EFull-auto merges only gate-green work a broken build could not fake; tiered blocks a core-path change for human sign-off
FA stranger runs the guide unaided; mixed-agent, mixed-size fleet completes a real wish unattended and grades honestly
§

Risks, each retired

Merge storms
Retired by fences (bp task frontier) + the serial merge arbiter. THE risk; addressed first-class in Waves A/E.
Runaway spend
Retired by the fleet-wide meter + spend-cap-as-zero-ambition (Wave D). Never bundle unbounded tokens.
Vacuous greens
Retired by the proof-must-fire obligation on every wave, and sealed grading in the orchestrator.
Fragile automation
Retired by disposability + lease-lapse recovery + durable runner (Wave D): kill and restart loses nothing.
Vendor lock
Already retired: provider-neutral core, Claude + Codex proven, one adapter line per new agent.
Neighbour noise
Retired at the machine boundary (Wave C): heavy work on a cloud support never touches the responsive main.
§

The sequence

ProvenCoreHardenSeal
Done · PoC + skills + router + Codex proof
A · Presence & roster
B · Efficiency loop
C · Cloud add-support
D · Durability & safety
E · Orchestrator at scale
F · The seal

Run each wave through bp-epic-cycle — the fleet builds itself the way it will build everything else — under the epic task task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5. Waves A and B are the shortest path to a fleet that is both visible and efficient; C–E can proceed in parallel once the roster exists.

§

Definition of done

  1. Join in one command. Any agent, any machine: fleet-run.sh listen <name> or the skill — and it appears in the roster.
  2. Conduct in one wish. Hand the orchestrator a goal; it decomposes, routes by size, dispatches, and grades — with nothing to babysit.
  3. Never a collision, never a runaway. Fences hold; the arbiter serialises; the spend cap brakes.
  4. Cloud and local are one. The same protocol, the same commands, the machine boundary the only real difference.
  5. Sealed by a real run. Wave F's unattended, mixed-agent, mixed-size proof — the epic closes on it.
The five ideas the whole plan rests on The ledger is the bus · a fence is a lease · presence is a heartbeat · the router is best-fit · the machine is the isolation boundary. Every wave is one of these five made more perfect. Nothing else is load-bearing.
